source: IPCC AR6 WG1 (2021) SPM A.4.4 & Ch.7.5; Otto et al. 2013; Lewis & Curry 2018
rationale: Equilibrium climate sensitivity: best estimate 3.0C, likely 2.5-4.0C, very likely 2.0-5.0C; right-skewed (cannot rule out >5C). Energy-balance studies (Otto 2013 ~2.0; Lewis & Curry 2018 ~1.6) are lower but now read as a lower bound (pattern effect). Independent check: the GIM T1.3 concentration-driven 1990-2023 backtest shows a clear temperature-RMSE minimum at ECS=3.0 once surface heat capacity is at its physical ~8 - matching AR6. Lognormal median 3.0, sigma 0.28 ~[2.0,4.9] 5-95%.

source: DICE-2016R2 (Nordhaus&Moffat 2017); Howard&Sterner 2017; Burke et al. 2015; GIM T1.4 cross-validation
rationale: Level-effect quadratic damage frac = coeff*T^2 (T above pre-industrial). Anchors (loss at 3C): DICE-2016R2 0.00236 (2.1%); GIM 0.006 (5.4%, ~2.5x DICE); Howard-Sterner pref. 0.0078-0.0089 (7-8%); +catastrophic 0.010-0.011 (9-10%); prior meta-analysis span 0.0021-0.0192 (1.9-17.3%). GIM sits within the empirical envelope, above DICE, below the Howard-Sterner preferred central. Growth-effect studies (Burke 2015 ~23%/2100; Kotz 2024 RETRACTED) imply a fatter upper tail not captured by a level multiplier, so the lognormal is right-skewed. See gim/damage_validation.py and docs/climate/DAMAGE_FUNCTION.md.
Small near-term warming co-benefit (agriculture/heating). Weak literature support; wide prior toward 0.
Warming (C above 2023 baseline) at which mild-warming benefit peaks; poorly constrained.
Multiplier amplifying damage for low-resilience actors; expert prior, wide.
Capital output elasticity = capital income share. Labor share 0.65-0.80 (Gollin) => capital share ~0.20-0.35; standard ~1/3.
Labor output elasticity. Gollin labor share 0.65-0.80; model calibrated 0.6 for its (non-CRS) production structure.
Energy output elasticity; small positive. Backtest-selected 0.042; literature aggregate energy share/elasticity ~0.03-0.08.
Aggregate capital depreciation ~4.0-4.2% (PWT, US 4.1% / China 3.1% 2011); range 3-8% across capital composition.

source: Geoffroy et al. 2013 two-layer EBM; GIM T1.3 joint recal
rationale: Two-box surface/upper-ocean heat capacity (model units). Geoffroy CMIP5 physical mean ~8. T1.3 joint multi-window recalibration sets production to 8 (was 18, a 2015-2023 short-window artifact that over-damped the transient and biased ECS to the 4C ceiling); paired with OCEAN_EXCHANGE=1.0 it improves both the 1990-2023 trend (temp RMSE 0.24->0.16) and the 2015-2023 levels (0.138->0.134). See docs/climate/CLIMATE_BACKTEST.md.
Deep-ocean heat capacity; slow thermal reservoir, weakly constrained.

source: Geoffroy et al. 2013; GIM T1.3 joint recal
rationale: Surface-deep ocean heat exchange coefficient. T1.3 joint recal sets production to 1.0 (was 0.7): with HEAT_CAP_SURFACE=8 the stronger heat uptake reconciles the 1990-2023 trend with the 2015-2023 levels (keeps short-window bias within +-0.02). Within Geoffroy gamma range.

source: GIM operational artifact / backtest; GCP2023 & WDI carbon-intensity trend
rationale: Structural decarbonisation calibration (compound, artifact-bound). Constrained: <0.031 fails historical CO2 envelope. Distinct from raw carbon-intensity decline (~1.5%/yr, GCP/WDI).
Data-derived emissions scaling bound to the compiled state; tight prior around the GCP-calibrated value.
Baseline crude birth rate (pre-GDP modifier). Global crude birth ~17/1000 (2023); model baseline 25/1000 reduced by prosperity terms.
Baseline crude death rate (pre-modifier). Global crude death ~8/1000 (2023).
Baseline real interest rate; neutral-rate (r*) estimates ~0.5-2.5%.

source: GIM backtest; endogenous-growth R&D elasticity literature
rationale: Sensitivity of TFP growth to R&D spending share; backtest-selected 0.3, wide prior.
eta: CRRA elasticity of marginal utility. Nordhaus 1.45, Stern 1.0; range spans the discounting debate.
rho: pure rate of time preference. Nordhaus ~1.5%/yr, Stern ~0.1%/yr; the central ethical-discounting parameter.

source: Burke et al. 2015; Kotz et al. 2024; Moore & Diaz 2015; GIM F4
rationale: Per-degC TFP-growth drag (growth-effect climate damage). 0.0 = level-effect-only (DICE / RFF-GIVE view); high = strong growth-effect (Burke/Kotz). At modern 2% discounting + 200y this maps SCC ~$184 (coeff 0) -> $314 (0.0003) -> $490 (0.0007), spanning the level-vs-growth 'catastrophic spread' as explicit sampled uncertainty. Production default 0.0 (conservative, level-only, golden-preserving); the prior lets the ensemble/SCC distribution explore the growth-effect upside. Mode near the low end reflects the unresolved level-vs-growth debate.

source: Global Carbon Project 2023; GIM emission-driven climate backtest
rationale: RESIDUAL land-use CO2 source (GtCO2/yr) beyond what EMISSIONS_SCALE already absorbs. GCB gross net LUC is ~4-5 GtCO2/yr, but EMISSIONS_SCALE=0.9755 implicitly contains most of it; the data-derived residual that closes the 1990-2023 CO2 gap (ppm_rmse 9.76->2.30) is ~0.6. Headline value 0.6 (E2.4 re-anchor); the gross value would double-count.

source: IPCC AR6 WG1 Ch.5; Schuur et al. 2015; McGuire et al. 2018
rationale: Permafrost/peat CO2 feedback flux, GtCO2/yr per degC warming above pre-industrial. AR6 assesses a positive but deeply uncertain permafrost carbon feedback (~14-19 GtC/degC cumulative to 2100); expressed here as a per-year flux ~0.4-3.7 GtCO2/yr at present-to-mid-century warming. Default 0 (off); wide right-skewed prior. ADDED on top of AR6 forced response (ECS 3.0), not a dilution of ECS.

source: IPCC AR6 WG1 Ch.5; Schuur et al. 2015
rationale: Permafrost CH4 feedback as a simplified steady-state extra forcing, W/m2 per degC warming. CH4 is short-lived (~12 yr) but high-GWP; modelled here as a forcing term rather than a dynamic CH4 pool (deferred). Small, very uncertain; default 0 (off).

source: van der Werf 2008 (Energy Economics); Koetse et al. 2008 meta-analysis; Stern 2012
rationale: Capital-energy substitution elasticity for the nested-CES (KLE) production core (F2.1). Empirical estimates cluster ~0.3-0.5 (gross complements). sigma=1 recovers Cobb-Douglas. Only active when PRODUCTION_FUNCTION='nested_ces' (re-anchor); default core is Cobb-Douglas (golden-preserving).

source: Labandeira et al. 2017 (energy demand elasticity meta-analysis); IMF/EIA
rationale: Price elasticity of resource (energy) demand for the F2.2 partial-clearing price rule. Short-run energy demand elasticity ~0.2-0.4, longer-run higher; gross-inelastic. Only active when MARKET_CLEARING=True (re-anchor); default uses the sluggish tatonnement (golden-preserving).
